# Binary merge factory binding

Genuine Kotlin introduces one method-owned Object-bounded T. Two fixed nominal
arguments remain independent of that formal. A complete binary callback consumes
T twice and returns T; the factory returns an invariant Box<T>. A raw invocation
must preserve all three callback slots, the original provider result and checks,
and the actual callback object. It cannot predict an invocation or returned value.

The frozen observer checks argument and callback identities, deferred callback
dispatch, typed bridges and casts, nulls, exact checked and unchecked failures,
and partial effects. Ten wrong programs must fail before NeverD runs. Source and
SDK-declaration profiles compile every emitted Java unit and compare all original
class/method identities, complete Signature, Exceptions and metadata. Only D8
CLASS annotations, source filenames and reported source helpers may differ.
